# Multitude IT Labs & GrowthBook | Recap, Pro vs. Enterprise and next steps - Meeting
Date: 2026-10-21 | Duration: 22.290000915527344m

## Summary
Legal and DPA reviews are underway, with a standard five-to-seven-day review SLA. The target signature date is October 28, although it could move to October 30, and internal approval remains required. The 15% discount and Net-45 payment terms depend on an October 28 commitment; Net-60 is available but is the maximum, with no further extension. Existing concessions include reduced ten-seat pricing, semiannual invoicing, and five-thousand-dollar seat pricing. The renewal term runs from October 28 through 2027 and uses an anniversary-based renewal date, but written commitment is still required. Legal may request DORA review, while the Trust Center link and available DORA coverage require verification. The contract package includes the DPA, customer agreement, and order form. The self-hosted purchase covers software, so service SLAs do not apply. The current need is ten seats, with additional seats available in five-seat packs, paid separately through invoicing, and no hard ceiling for enterprise expansion. GrowthBook provides dedicated response coverage, same-day turnaround, and possible responses within a few hours.

# Multitude IT Labs & GrowthBook | Recap, Pro vs. Enterprise and next steps - Legal Review Responses
Date: 2026-10-28 | Duration: 14.720000267028809m

## Summary
Legal review is complete, with limited modifications covering payment, invoicing, and the confirmed start date. Payment terms were set at 60 days instead of the previously discussed 45 days, and Multitude IT Labs was identified as the customer party. The agreement is scheduled to begin on November 1, 2026, with signatures targeted this week. The PQQ submission was received, and its blank format was accepted, allowing review to begin; however, signatory authority evidence for Ryan McKirk remained a blocker because no official stamped document was provided. DORA classification is still pending, with ICT non-critical status being considered and a possible removal of the DORA requirement awaiting confirmation from the Multitude team. Ryan Kirk was confirmed as the customer signatory, while Multitude will initiate DocuSign. Pricing is already discounted to $500 annually per user from $1,000, with no further discount currently available; tier and expansion pricing may be revisited as adoption increases.
